Document processing

Felican IDP

Intelligent Document Processor. Reads the documents your business runs on — invoices, contracts, forms, receipts — and turns them into structured, usable data.

Ask about Felican IDPBook a call
Input
Invoices, contracts, forms, receipts, PDFs, scans
Output
Structured fields, validated, in the format your system expects

Classification and routing
Where it runs
Cloud or fully private, same as Private AI

What it actually is

Somewhere in your business a person is retyping numbers from a PDF into a system. Felican IDP is the thing that stops that.

It reads a document, works out what kind of document it is, extracts the fields that matter, validates them, and hands clean structured data to whatever you already use. No template setup for every new vendor layout, because it reads the document rather than matching coordinates on a page.

Who this is for

  • Anyone with an accounts payable pile. Invoices arrive in a hundred layouts and every one gets keyed by hand.
  • Distribution and logistics — packing lists, bills of lading, freight invoices, all arriving as scans.
  • Contractors and trades reconciling supplier invoices against job costs.
  • Practices handling intake forms where the information is on paper and needed in a system.
  • Any business where a contract clause matters and nobody has time to read every renewal.

What it does, specifically

  • Extracts fields — vendor, dates, line items, totals, tax, terms, party names, clause text — across layouts it has never seen.
  • Classifies and routes. An invoice goes to AP, a signed contract goes to the file, an intake form starts a workflow.
  • Validates. Line items that do not sum to the total, a date that cannot be right, a vendor that is not on file — these get flagged rather than silently passed on.
  • Flags low confidence for review instead of guessing. A human checks the handful that need checking rather than all of them.
  • Hands off clean data to your accounting, ERP or document system.

Why this is the honest use of AI

Document extraction is one of the few AI applications where the business case does not require any optimism. The task is well defined, the output is checkable, the error mode is visible, and the thing it replaces is measurably slow and dull.

It is also the place where AI verification earns its keep, which is why CrossCheck AI exists — when a number is going to drive a payment, having a second model confirm the first is cheap insurance.

What determines the cost

  • Volume. Documents per month is the main driver.
  • Document variety. One form type is simple. Forty vendor invoice layouts plus contracts plus receipts is a bigger configuration job.
  • Where it runs. Private deployment costs more to stand up and nothing per document after that.
  • How deep the write-back goes. Producing a validated export is straightforward. Posting directly into your ERP is an integration project.

Questions people actually ask

Before you call

How accurate is the extraction?

Accuracy depends on document quality and type, and anyone quoting you a single percentage without seeing your documents is guessing. The practical answer is that the system reports its own confidence, low-confidence fields go to a human, and we measure real accuracy on your documents during the pilot before you commit to anything. If it does not beat your current process on your own paperwork, it is not worth buying.

Do we need to set up a template for every vendor?

No, and that is the main difference from older OCR tooling. It reads documents rather than matching fixed positions, so a new vendor layout works without configuration.

Can it handle handwriting and bad scans?

Printed text and clean scans are reliable. Handwriting and poor photocopies are harder and get flagged for review more often. We test with your actual worst documents, not a clean sample.

Can this run without documents leaving our network?

Yes. Felican IDP can deploy on the same private footing as Private AI, which is usually the requirement when the documents are contracts or patient records.
